content.text: VerdBoard Documentation

VerdBoard (青编) combines whiteboards, mind maps, workflows, architecture diagrams, UML class/sequence diagrams and standalone rich-text documents. Open the repository's root workspace folder in the desktop application to read and edit the project documentation together with its native diagrams.

This workspace documents the current source as of 2026-10-28: two applications and 22 public packages. Breaking plugin and Action changes are recorded in pending major Changesets; the 2.0 release and dated acceptance records remain historical.
Automatic layout and connector routing
Layout algorithms
Routing algorithms
Automatic calculation

The ninth native topic diagram explains scope selection, scene-specific node layout, orthogonal obstacle routing, bounded route optimization and atomic commits. Ordinary automatic routes stay in memory; explicit optimization stores editable waypoints. Both automatic switches default to off, remember a fixed scope only for the session, and merge their results into the triggering edit. Drag/resize/rotation previews reuse settled routes; camera pan and zoom do not trigger layout.

Return-to-source and reference locations preserve reading context. Navigation feedback waits for the actual view and target; save feedback combines the active file and its referenced sources without treating navigation metadata as a content save.

Dated acceptance records

The Chinese navigation and this English introduction are maintained together. Detailed engineering documentation is primarily Chinese. Native .verd-doc.json files are the sole maintained documentation source; there is no generated Markdown compatibility tree.
UML diagrams

UML Class Diagram and UML Sequence Diagram are native FrameCanvas domains. Classifiers, members, relationships, multiplicities, participants, ordered messages, activations, notes and nested alt/opt/loop fragments are editable. Mermaid import/export preserves semantic structure; native JSON preserves the complete document.
Application appearance

Web and Desktop offer Light, Dark, and System under My → Settings → General, following the system by default. Device preferences apply immediately across workspaces and synchronize between windows. Interface chrome, standalone documents, canvases and embedded documents adapt to the appearance. Each canvas selects one theme with light and dark variants. Authored custom colors and images are preserved; image exports offer Current appearance, Light and Dark. Switching appearance does not edit files or create undo history.
Schema-driven settings

Application preferences, workspace settings and ordinary inspector fields use a lightweight, separately maintained Settings SDK. Host transactions, history, inheritance, existing controls and commit timing remain authoritative. The native architecture, source index and development guide describe the migration inventory and reproducible tarball integration. SDK publication and registry-only verification remain release gates.
Next major: actions and stable element links

The current source shares action definitions between toolbars, menus, keyboard shortcuts, command palettes and help. Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+P opens the nearest editor scope. @sue/board-react-actions depends only on common and React, so standalone documents do not pull in the board renderer.

WorkspaceTarget links address a file, heading or one Cell. Cell identity is globally unique and follows moves; the URL file ID is a hint. Navigation waits for the source commit receipt and target layout, supports cancellation and return-to-source, and temporarily reveals collapsed Mind ancestors without saving or changing undo history. Exports use canonical layout.

Controller mutation methods and plugin-local keyboard dispatch are replaced by getActionState/executeAction/actions. revealTarget replaces one-way reveal props; DocumentEditor exposes awaitable flushEditing and host receipts. The native React integration and migration documents describe the breaking contracts. This work prepares major Changesets only and does not bump versions or publish.

Node layout and edge rerouting are separate actions. Layout supports selected objects, direct Group contents and the current focused container; nested groups remain rigid. Whiteboards also offer connection-based layout with cycle support. Rerouting resets authored orthogonal paths without moving nodes or changing ports, anchors, straight lines or curves. Conflicting layouts leave the document unchanged, and each applied action is one undo step. See the native arrangement and grouping guide for the scope rules and planner APIs.
Quick Start
Requirements: Node.js >= 22 and pnpm >= 11.18.0. Root package.json, package manifests and pnpm-lock.yaml define the actual commands and dependency versions.

pnpm install
pnpm dev:desktop
# Web development
pnpm dev:web
# Public packages and Web; excludes Desktop
pnpm build
# Desktop frontend, main process and preload
pnpm build:desktop
# Validated installer; macOS defaults to DMG, add --with-zip for ZIP
pnpm package:desktop
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test

Run pnpm dev:desktop (also pnpm dev / pnpm start) for source-based development. VerdBoard Dev uses appData/VerdBoard Dev and a persistent workspaces/default copy seeded once from repository native files, excluding runtime metadata. It never imports the old desktop selection. Open the repository workspace explicitly to maintain project documentation. Production retains appData/VerdBoard and its legacy recovery. Explicit data/workspace environment overrides remain available. Daily development and tests never package, install, register or close the production application.
Workspace Architecture

WorkspaceApp opens a WorkspaceHost. WorkspaceSession owns file identities, commands, shared history, validation, external-change conflicts and conditional persistence. Canvas files (.verd.json, FrameFileV2) are assembled into one CellStore and rendered by VerdFrame → FrameCanvas → CellRuntime. Standalone documents (.verd-doc.json, DocumentFileV1) keep a BoardTextDocument body and use DocumentPage/DocumentEditor; they are peer workspace files, rather than Cells in the canvas store.

Canvas references target stable file identities. Diagram ownership and canvas references are independent: a diagram may belong to one whiteboard while appearing in multiple references. Documents use verd://file/encoded-file-id#encoded-heading-slug links for workspace navigation. Heading anchors follow GitHub's slug and duplicate-heading rules.

Desktop uses real directories, conditional writes and recoverable transaction journals. Web uses an IndexedDB workspace host. The shared session validates candidate file changes before committing them, groups related text edits into one undo step and reports failed saves for retry. Desktop waits for flush on shutdown; browser exit flushing remains best effort.
Features
Mind maps: nine layouts, topic reparenting, collapse, images, emoji, rich-text notes, summaries, file-level color schemes and automatic content sizing with a default maximum width of 240.
Workflows: native start/task/decision Cells, ports, DAG and process modes, validated connections and explicit layouts.
Architecture diagrams: ordered layers, modules, dependencies, placement and shared orthogonal routing.
Whiteboard: geometry, hand-drawn paths, connectors, images, tables, swimlanes, freehand and editable polylines.
Shared interactions: alignment, equal-gap distribution, drag guides, nested groups, locking, rich-text styling, clipboard and image export.
Documents: headings, lists, tables, code, links and images, find/replace, outline navigation, Markdown import/export and native JSON export.

Presentation: a separate read-only fullscreen view of the current canvas with overview, object focus, structured mind-map/layer steps and a laser pointer. Use 0 for overview, L for the pointer and Esc to exit. Presentation state remains in memory.
Extension Boundaries

For a complete editor, compose create*UIPlugin factories with FrameEditor. Lower-level hosts build createFramePluginSet(plugins) and pass pluginSet to FrameCanvas, using value/onChange or adapter/onIntent. Engine-only callers use createCellRegistry({plugins}); legacy extension factories require the corresponding engine plugin to be installed first. Domain React packages expose explicit style.css entries. The old domain Canvas components remain removed. DocumentEditor uses BoardTextDocument and its shared ActionController.

The current dependency families are React 19, TypeScript 6, Vite 6, pnpm 11, TipTap 3 and Electron 28. Daily Desktop E2E uses pnpm test:e2e:desktop with real Vite and temporary data. For production acceptance, run pnpm build:desktop then pnpm test:e2e:desktop:prod. Packaged tests have a separate configuration and run only in the explicit packaging workflow. Dated test counts in historical records describe those runs, not the current checkout.
Last updated: 2026-10-28.

Document Frames in a general canvas edit the same standalone source document (double-click to edit, Escape to leave). Read-only document references remain available in every canvas. Each project topic diagram includes its related document and stable section links.

Workspace folders move to trash as one entry and restore with their nested files and empty directories. Trash supports confirmed permanent deletion and emptying only the selected entries. Open My from the sidebar or canvas More menu. My contains device preferences. Workspace settings default to General and provide a separate Trash section for the current workspace. Open workspace settings and Desktop folder actions from the workspace-name menu at the top of the sidebar. Preferences keep their existing device storage and apply immediately.

The file tree shows every canvas, diagram and document at its actual workspace path, including owned and unorganized charts. Owner canvases also provide marked shortcuts with Open and Show in folder actions. Both entries open the same source and reuse its editor and tab. The chart library can change ownership of an existing specialized chart without moving its file.
npm 2.0.0 integration
2.0 integration and migration

All 20 public packages release as 2.0.0 to the configured Aliyun registries. Migrate VerdBoardApp(adapter) to WorkspaceApp(host); FrameCanvas already exists in 1.0. Package READMEs include registry setup, runnable examples and CSS entrypoints.
Next major: explicit engine and UI plugins

The next major version introduces explicit CellPlugin and FrameUIPlugin composition for Draw, Mind, Workflow, Architecture and UML. Minimal embedding uses core, one domain engine, React core and its domain UI. Rich text remains built in; converters and product packages are optional. Missing kinds reject the entire file without normalization or writes. File formats stay FrameFileV2/DocumentFileV1. See the next-major sections in Architecture and React integration. This task does not bump or publish packages.
One-shot layout and session automatic calculation

Layout nodes and Optimize all edges run once. Auto layout nodes and Auto optimize edges are independent switches, initially off. Enabling a switch only affects later edits, captures the current Frame, Group or selection, and does not create a save or undo entry. The workspace remembers each file/Frame setting across tab switches; closing the last corresponding tab or restarting clears it. Nothing is persisted in document data.

Node automation reacts to additions, deletions, relationship changes and resizing; manual movement keeps its position. During dragging, resizing and rotation, previews are coalesced to animation frames and only adjust connected endpoints. Full routing optimization, crossing bridges and label avoidance wait until the gesture ends. When both switches are enabled, node layout precedes edge optimization and all derived changes join the initiating edit in one atomic transaction and undo step. Host rejection or layout conflicts leave the source unchanged; loading, host echoes and undo/redo do not trigger automation.

One-shot edge optimization saves existing orthogonal paths with editable points, preserving terminals, ports, anchors, labels and appearance. Reloading preserves the result. With automatic edge optimization off, later movement adjusts the adjoining endpoint legs. Legacy route.strategy: optimized remains readable but no longer enables continuous work. FrameCanvas accepts optional autoCalculation and onAutoCalculationChange; FrameAutoCalculationProvider shares runtime settings across instances. No document migration is required.

Routing-stage measurements on 2026-10-28 (three preview frames per fixture, excluding complete UI rendering): 41-edge package diagram, 69.02ms to 0.44ms per frame; 60-node/120-edge dense diagram, 107.84ms to 0.26ms. These are diagnostic timings, not frame-rate guarantees. Regression tests assert coalescing, no full optimization during previews, atomic history, host rejection and persistence.

Edge routing uses a joined split button with a shared border. The arrow only opens the menu; selecting an available menu item immediately executes that action once and remembers it for the main button across inspector and context menu. Selecting the current method runs it again. Disabled items remain focusable to explain why they are unavailable, without changing the choice. The arrow stays available when the main action is disabled. Pending actions block duplicate execution across both surfaces; a rejected action retains the selected method for retry. Reset manual paths clears all saved points, including optimized points, and restores ordinary automatic routing. Optimize all edges recalculates the current scope and saves editable paths. Neither action moves nodes or changes the automatic-calculation switches. Mode selection adds no history; changed paths use one undo step and unchanged results add none.

Manual dev uses port 7300 and dist-electron-dev; dev E2E owns port 7310, a separate Vite cache and dist-electron-e2e. Production builds retain dist-electron. E2E never reuses or closes a manual dev instance.

Canvas Frames use live vector previews and activate one editor on double-click. A bounded HTML-to-SVG paint host isolates preview rendering; exports keep the shared scene as flat SVG. Viewport snapshots avoid per-wheel layout reads without changing native DPR or content quality. See the native acceptance record for five-run performance results and the conditional Desktop runtime decision.

Diagram colors follow the selected theme in both appearances across UML, workflow, architecture, Mind, drawing, tables and swimlanes. Unmarked legacy colors are theme-controlled; only per-field custom sources lock literal colors. Transparent layers, authored rich-text colors and manually selected Mind schemes retain their meaning. Mermaid imports mark only explicit style/classDef/linkStyle declarations as custom, including multiple classes and default declarations. Switching appearance derives presentation without rewriting files or undo history.
Two-level system guide

Read Project Guide → nine topic overviews → twenty-one mechanism detail diagrams. Overviews explain responsibilities and relationships; details cover the main flow, failure branches, persistence boundaries and source entrypoints.
Open Project Guide

Detail diagrams live under 架构图/细节, grouped by topic. Overviews are regular canvases that embed detail references; detail diagrams retain their architecture, workflow or mind-map scenes. Source navigation returns one level at a time and restores the reading position.
